title: Portugal applies to join the EEC
summary: The first constitutional government, led by Mário Soares, submitted Portugal's application for membership of the European Economic Community on 28 March 1977, eleven months after the constitution came into force. The application was as much political as economic: accession was a way of anchoring a democracy that had almost not survived 1975, and of choosing Europe over the alternatives the revolutionary period had put on the table. Negotiations opened in 1978 and took until 1985, held up by the Community's own agricultural and budgetary disputes as much as by Portugal. It is in the atlas as the first step of the process that ends with accession in 1986.
